amend.summary:
All 41 slice-path blocker and major findings (P3 and SL1) are decided and applied to rewrite/spec/: 38 fixed, 3 left-for-builder, none rejected. About 90 spec files changed; nothing under next/, rewrite/history/, rewrite/tools/ or README was edited, and rewrite/spec/packages/ changed only through gen_packages.py.

The five subjects several reviewers raised:
- Local delivery (commands/story-deliver.md, one place): the merge commit is made in the integration worktree, which is always detached; the branch is then moved by update-ref when checked out nowhere, or by `git merge --ff-only` in the checkout that holds it, the one stated exception to never touching the person's checkout. A refused fast-forward returns a new state, `checkout_dirty`, with nothing moved. Keeping the integration branch out of the person's checkout (P3REQ-10's proposal) was not taken: too high touch.
- Verdict recomputation (topics/verdicts.md): the step identity carries `method`, and `loop` and `pass` on review, fix and arbitrate steps; step names include the loop so a re-review overwrites nothing; the file defines which records are passes and every input the tool rebuilds.
- Red evidence and the merge guard: the green gate and delivery require a red record; step-results blocks a passing gate result with no matching evidence record; tests-first covers Bash writes; merge-guard blocks ref-moving commands for every caller; a closed git-read family plus a catch-all git-other; an absent `commands` key means none.
- Gate behaviour (commands/gate-red.md, gate-green.md, topics/gates.md): test identity, base report, red versus error, exemptions, test file, stub marker VSDD-STUB, the ac<N> criterion map, and a clean-worktree rule.
- The cycle's base (topics/worktrees.md): there is none; each story records the commit it was cut from as delivery.base in its closure.

One thing added: schema `implement-data` (registered in registry.d/amend.toml), needed because a script may read only required fields. No command, record, rule, agent or package was added; the build-order corrections are rules and a slice milestone in packaging/build-plan.md, because package briefs are generated from the blueprint in history.

Built code under next/ that must now follow the design:
- left-for-builder: launch.sh cli branch must pass vsdd's exit 1 through silently (SL1-03); events.py EVENT_SCHEMA must admit launcher-written lines, null session_id and whole-second ts (SL1-05); build.py must generate every S_* literal from schema files and C1 must add the survey, checkpoint-result, delivery-data, story-unit, wave-gate-data and implement-data files (SL1-06).
- consequences of P3 fixes: step-result schema, fixtures and prelude step() gain `method`/`loop`/`pass`; judge() gains the `grounded !== false` test; converge() passes `pass` to arbitrate; relay() uses the empty-object fallback; S_SURVEY, S_CLOSE and S_DELIVERY require every field.

Open platform dependency: whether `updatedInput` is honoured on a StructuredOutput call (item 27's probe now covers it); the design states what happens either way. rewrite/STATE.md was not edited: its layer 2 package list should be corrected from packaging/build-plan.md.

resolutions.what_was_done: The step identity now carries `method` (required) and, for review, fix and arbitrate steps, `loop` and `pass`; the tool reads those fields and never parses a step name. A review record is a done record with a pass whose method belongs to a reviewer-tier agent and whose stored agent type is that owner. The built step-result schema, its fixtures and the prelude's step() under next/ must follow.

resolutions.what_was_done: There is no cycle base. A story branch is cut from the head of the branch it will be delivered to, read when the branch is created (the integration branch, its remote head after a fetch in pr mode; hotfix/<version>, created at the release tag, in a hotfix cycle). The worktree library records it as delivery.base in the story's closure record, and the descent check, the red comparison and the green diff use that recorded commit. Recording it in the run record as well was not taken: the closure is tracked and is what a resumed run reads.

An absent `commands` key means none (stricter than the proposed git-read default); builders hold git-commit and git-read, the codebase-analyzer git-read, the spike-runner git-commit, git-read and git-other, the main session every family.

resolutions.what_was_done: One local-delivery rule, as proposed except for the dirty case: detached merge in the integration worktree, then update-ref or a fast-forward of the checkout that holds the branch. A refused fast-forward returns `checkout_dirty` (blocked, no decision the first time, rerun after cleaning) instead of awaiting_merge, because a merge decision cannot clean a checkout and would cost the person a second command. `vsdd release` moves its branch the same way; the delivery tests cover the checkout clean, overlapping, non-overlapping, absent and moved.

Rules never test the payload cwd alone: `where`, the call's effective directory (the target's directory, or the directory a cd, git -C or vsdd -C names), defines the caller's worktree. The lock is refreshed only by calls that belong to the run (a vsdd call with its --run, a StructuredOutput with its step.run, a call in its worktrees, a subagent call in the holder's session). If updatedInput is not honoured the marker is found by a hash of the call's arguments, oldest unread first, so item 29 no longer gates anything but the offered cut.

A survey from the holder's own session for the same workflow and subject re-enters the run when it has no step record and otherwise ends it and takes over; `ended` in the run record defines a live run, and pipeline commands refuse one that is not. `vsdd lock release` frees the caller's own session's lock or a stale one; --force (person) any.

resolutions.what_was_done: Adopted `checkout_dirty` as the state for a checkout the merge would overwrite, but not merging in the person's checkout: the merge commit is always made in the tool's detached integration worktree, so a conflict never lands in the person's files, and their checkout only ever receives a fast-forward that git refuses atomically. The invariant wording is amended; init and doctor need no change because the checkout on the integration branch is the normal, supported case.

merge-guard now blocks, for every caller, commands that move, replace or delete the integration or release branch without a checkout (update-ref, symbolic-ref, branch -f/-m/-M/-c/-C/-d/-D, switch -C, checkout -B, fetch, pull and push refspecs). Those commands sit in the new git-other family, which no builder holds. The proposed integration_moved refusal was not taken: a person in local mode, and other people's merges in pr mode, move the branch legitimately; local delivery re-merges from the new head instead.

`method` is in the step identity and so in every step record; a pass counts only when its method belongs to a reviewer-tier agent in the methods table and the stored agent type is that owner. A conformance fixture has a builder echo a reviewer's method.

Each rule module is imported inside its own rule's try, so an import error is that rule's rule.error and the quarantine condition can be met. The rule_error block's fix line names the restart with VSDD_FACTORY_HOOKS_QUARANTINE=<rule>, and the briefing's state-problems line and vsdd status list rules with repeated rule.error. Copying block codes into a blocked packet was not taken: the briefing line already reaches the person.

Resolved by the local-delivery rule in story-deliver, not by the proposal. Keeping the integration branch out of the person's checkout was rejected: it makes a person leave their own branch in every project with no remote and merge by hand to see delivered work, which is high touch. The checkout on the integration branch is the supported case, so init, doctor and the sample need no special handling, and the slice fixture keeps the checkout on that branch.

The step identity carries method, loop and pass; story.js names review, fix and arbitrate steps with the loop and pass (review-<lens>-l<n>-p<k>), so a scoped re-review writes new records. verdicts.md now defines what the tool rebuilds: passes, items to account for, disputes, rulings, waivers, the cap and `used`, the order of loops across runs, and when a verdict covers a head; the conformance table gains a case per input.

resolutions.what_was_done: The mechanism is specified once, as proposed in steps 1 to 3 (detached merge, ref moved from the old head only, fast-forward of a checkout that holds the branch as the one exception). Step 4 differs: a refused fast-forward returns `checkout_dirty`, not awaiting_merge, and git itself decides (it refuses only when a local change would be overwritten).

judge() and its Python copy treat `grounded === false` as not hard, and on a step's second return step-results returns updatedInput with the mark so the script judges what the tool stored. Whether updatedInput is honoured on a StructuredOutput call is unproven: item 27's probe now covers it (B8 must run it), and where it is not honoured the design says the tool's verdict stands, the checkpoint records the stage from it and the next run continues from `reviewed`. Blocking a second time was not taken, because it can use up the platform's retries and lose the pass.

A passing record for the head is returned without measuring again; a failing one never is. `vsdd init` lists files its trial runs left untracked and not ignored.

The run, cycle, closure, decision and evidence records now have typed schemas with required lists: the evidence record has sha, patch_id, passed, and for red `frozen` ({file, sha256}), `tests` and `criteria`; the run record has `stories`, `amendment` and `ended`; the closure has delivery.branch and delivery.base. No package E0 was added: the plan says E1 is built in two parts and the first needs only B3 and S1.

The order is fixed by rules in the build plan, with no new package: B6 and C2 before layer 2, H1 and S2b after the B8 items that decide their code, S4 in the slice (so H7 is not split), and the sample, fixtures and loader ahead of the rest of E1. The slice is recorded there as the first milestone in six ordered steps. The package briefs are generated from the blueprint in history and could not be edited, so where a brief and a rule differ the plan says the rule holds.

The plan states that a workflow needs the package of every agent its script names (W2 and W3 need A2b; W7 needs A2b and A6b; W11 and W12 need A6b). The roster keeps listing the whole design, so the prelude's tier tables are complete; until every package is built L-ROSTER enforces only `none extra`. The slice ships every agent file story.js names, each complete with only the methods the story script gives it.

S3 is not split into two packages; the plan orders it in two parts (records, preconditions, route, worktrees, admission and cycles first; positions, re-measuring and the checkpoint mapping after G2 and G3), and the survey reaches gates through a gate registry in the evidence store, which removes the S3 and G5 cycle. The six story positions are defined from records and git.

Ctx gains `where`, the effective directory of a call (the target's directory; for a Bash segment the directory of a cd, git -C or vsdd -C, else cwd), and `story`, `in_spike`, merge-guard, auto-allow and liveness use it. The two cases are stated: `cd <story worktree> && git commit` with the main checkout on the integration branch is allowed, and a bare `git commit` there is blocked.

The implement step has a data schema, implement-data, that requires test_defects. An implementer that finds a frozen test wrong returns blocked with the list; story.js then runs one test-writer step (test-defects, method test-fixes, ending with gate red --refreeze) and the implement step once more. A new schema was needed because a script may only read required fields; it is registered in registry.d/amend.toml.

resolutions.what_was_done: The design now says what was built: the Playwright entry carries no option, because the pinned server refuses file: addresses by default; L-MCP rejects --allow-unrestricted-file-access; probe 33 confirms the default on the running server.

The discriminator the launcher uses is now in the design: on uv exit 2 only, it runs `uv python find --no-python-downloads '>=3.11'` with a cache of its own; an interpreter found means uv is at fault (uv_unusable), none means the Python floor (py_floor).

The design now says neither entry execs uv, and gives the cli entry's exit mapping: 0 and 1 pass through silently, 2 runs the interpreter probe and adds the uv fix only when no Python is found, any other code is reported. The code is wrong on one point: in next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/launch.sh the cli branch's `*)` case prints `the vsdd tool could not run (exit 1)` for vsdd's own negative answer; it needs a `1) exit 1 ;;` case before it, with a test.

The contents of next/.gitignore are specified as built: /.mcp.json with the negation !/plugins/vsdd-factory/.mcp.json, .claude/worktrees/, /.worktrees/, settings.local.json, caches and node_modules, with the reason the negation is needed during the rewrite.

The design now says the launcher writes runner.launch_failed and runner.disabled itself, with v, ts in whole seconds, type, severity, session_id null, code and mode, into the same directory and honouring VSDD_EVENTS_DIR; the event schema admits a null session_id and both timestamp forms. The launcher matches. events.py does not: EVENT_SCHEMA in next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/events.py requires a non-empty string session_id and a millisecond timestamp, so the schema it prints rejects the launcher's lines; it must accept null and whole seconds for reading while the Python writer keeps writing its own strict form.

The design now states that every shape (step result, step data, tool outputs, records) is a schema file under <plugin>/schemas/ delivered by C1, and that every S_* literal in the prelude is generated from its file. The code does not do this yet: next/workflow-lib/prelude.js writes S_REVIEW, S_FIXES, S_RULINGS, S_HOLDOUT, S_SURVEY, S_CLOSE, S_DELIVERY and S_WAVE_GATE by hand, and next/plugins/vsdd-factory/schemas/ has no survey, checkpoint-result, delivery-data, story-unit, wave-gate-data or implement-data file. C1 must add those files and tools/build.py must generate the literals and fail --check on a hand-written one.

The reader's semantics are pinned as built: refused, not misread. On every input it accepts it equals PyYAML's YAML 1.1 safe_load, and every plain scalar YAML 1.1 would retype is refused with the line number. The differential test is extended to artifact frontmatter in the fixture overlays and hook case files and to a corpus of inputs that must be refused; the first of these is added to the built test when those fixtures exist.

enc() is specified as built: encodeURIComponent plus the five characters it leaves raw (! ' ( ) *). Universal test 11 passes a request with both quotes, a semicolon, parentheses, an asterisk and an exclamation mark and requires that none appears raw.

The holdout finding's shape is settled as built: location is {"path": ""}, owner is product-owner, and holdoutFindings(unit, scores, opts) takes its thresholds from the survey's config.holdout (not limits) and its spec_ref and seed from a new `holdout` field (seed, contracts by scenario) in the output of gate wave and gate release, because only the tool can read a scenario.

The harness table now lists what the builder implemented: log(), budget.total and remaining(), pipeline(items, ...stages) with stages receiving (prev, item, index), workflow() returning the child's value and throwing when it threw, agents counted and workflow() calls not; and the schema rule is corrected to `required` optional and a subset of properties.

Universal tests 4, 5 and 7 now say that every stub returns as `step` the identity its prompt gave it and that the survey stub passes with the units the test supplies, which is what the built tests do; test 4 also asserts that the loops ran.

The checkpoint output is typed: ok and error, plus status, progress, decisions and next exactly as the workflow-result schema types them, all required. The built S_CLOSE has the same types; its required list (ok, status, next) grows to all six when the literals are generated from the schema files.

verify.summary:
I checked 79 entries: 38 from the tables repair and 41 from the slice amendment. 61 are sound. Not clean: 7 major problems remain from the entries, and 4 new major problems were caused or left by the fixes. None of them is on the slice's happy path (one story, local mode, no repair).

- Both checks pass. spec_lint prints "0 problem(s)". sections coverage prints "240 sections; 181 cited; 39 retired; 0 uncovered".
- Twelve table entries were only partly done: the tables were fixed but the prose copies they name were not. Every artifact file still restates its row (AU-T2-08). project-configuration.md still calls its example "the one key list, with its default", and that example disagrees with config-keys.toml (AU-S2-03 with T2-13, T2-15, P3SEAM-06). Pointers into the originals and second definitions of tables remain in prose. The scenario kind name was not settled.
- New major problems from the amendment:
  1. A rebase in pr mode makes the red record unreachable and changes the patch id against the fixed recorded base (VSA-01).
  2. delivery-data's "ok" is false for ci_failed, conflict and review_stale, so story.js never repairs (VSA-02).
  3. After a repair, the tool and the script account for different files in the later review loop (VSA-03).
  4. Defining the caller's worktree by the effective directory "in any rule" empties own-worktree, the spike runner's only write grant (VSA-04).
- The three left-for-builder entries (SL1-03, SL1-05, SL1-06) were correctly left. The code under next/ differs exactly as stated.
- build-plan.md's slice list now adds B8, C2, B6, S4, B4b, the first part of E1, A2b and A5, so STATE.md is out of date.

remaining.problem: Caused by P3SEAM-03 and P3OPS-02. Every measure now uses the fixed recorded base; patch_id is the diff from that base; delivery and green require a red record on a commit between the base and the head. story-deliver still rebases in pr mode and claims the patch id survives a clean rebase. After a rebase the red record's commit is not an ancestor of the head, so delivery refuses and green fails 'no red record'. The diff also includes stories merged meanwhile, so the patch id changes and every rebase goes review_stale.
remaining.where: topics/worktrees.md (The base of a story branch); topics/evidence-lookup.md; commands/story-deliver.md (What it refuses, verdict binding); commands/gate-green.md; records/evidence.md
remaining.proposed_resolution: On a rebase, delivery re-records delivery.base as the commit it rebased onto. The red lookup also accepts the latest red or re-freeze record whose frozen files' SHA-256 match the head and whose patch id equals the head's diff from the new base. State this once in worktrees.md and evidence-lookup.md. Add a G4a fixture: pr mode, integration moved, clean rebase, merged with no re-review.

remaining.problem: delivery-data.schema.json, rewritten in this pass, says ok is 'False when the story was not merged and no person is being waited for', so ok is false for ci_failed, conflict and review_stale. story.js tests !d.ok first and returns blocked, so the delivery repair loop never runs.
remaining.proposed_resolution: Define ok as 'the command ran and reached a state': false only for refused, checkout_dirty and a command that could not run. List the ok value of each state in story-deliver.md.

remaining.problem: Caused by P3BLD-01. In a later review loop, verdicts.md takes the items to account for as the files changed from the converged commit to the reviewed head. story.js passes d.changed_files, which delivery computed before the repair commits, and delivery-data never defines changed_files. After a ci_failed or conflict repair the tool's list holds files the reviewers were not asked about, so the tool's verdict is not converged while the script's is, and delivery refuses.
remaining.where: topics/verdicts.md (Items to account for); topics/story-script.md (review(round + 1, d.reviewed_sha, 2, d.changed_files, 0)); schemas/delivery-data.schema.json
remaining.proposed_resolution: Define changed_files as the files changed from reviewed_sha to the delivered head. After a repair, take the list from the gate green --since result (add changed_files to it). Use the same definition in the tool. Add a conformance fixture in which a repair touches a new file.

remaining.problem: Caused by P3BLD-12 and P3COV-02. rule-model.md says 'the caller's worktree' and related phrases mean, in any rule, the worktree containing `where` (for a file tool, the target's own directory).
